sections.h2: Selling a house in Aberdeen, South Dakota
sections.html:
Brown County's seat sits in the James River valley, in the northeast corner of the state. Only Sioux Falls and Rapid City are bigger. Slow-moving Moccasin Creek winds through town, and the first Milwaukee Road train rolled in on July 6, 1881, the day the city was founded.

The 2020 census counted 28,495 residents. An estimate for 2025 puts the number at 27,961, which is 1.8 percent under the 2020 base of 28,479. Keep that gentle decline in mind as you weigh a listing price against a cash offer.

Housing measureAberdeen, 2020 to 2024
Households12,469
Owner-occupied housing rate61.7%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$217,300
Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage$1,524
Median monthly owner cost without a mortgage$584
Median gross rent$762

Summers run hot and winters run cold and dry. A January day averages 12.8 degrees Fahrenheit, roughly 38 days a year dip below zero, and snow adds up to about 42 inches. Minus 46 in 1912 is the record low.

  • Furnaces fail in cold snaps, and an empty house with no heat can freeze, so keep the thermostat on.
  • Heavy snow tests roofs and gutters.
  • Freeze and thaw swings can crack basement walls and foundations, a favorite subject for home inspectors.

Branches down after a storm? We don't need the yard cleaned up first.

If the house sits empty, look first at the city's Nuisance Vacant Building rules. An ordinance declares certain vacant buildings a public nuisance and sets up a registration program, spelling out owner duties, enforcement and penalties. A new registration carries a $1,000 annual fee on the city's fee schedule.

Building Inspection, Code Enforcement and a Residential Contractor Board are also city departments. Phone the city about an empty inherited house to learn if it was flagged and which repairs would lift the flag.

  • Vacant houses can attract code enforcement.
  • A cash buyer can take an inherited or rented house in its present state.
  • Before closing, the title company checks for city charges tied to the property.

Brown County handles both taxes and recording for Aberdeen. Visit the Treasurer at 25 Market St., Suite 2, Aberdeen, SD 57401, or call (605) 626-7133. Weekday hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., though title transfers can't begin after 4:45 p.m. That office bills property tax for the county, the city, school districts and other taxing districts, and it runs tax aid for low-income and elderly families.

Deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, easements and similar papers are filed with the Register of Deeds, whose land records reach back to the early 1870s. Legal opinions aren't offered there; staff point people to an abstractor, title company or attorney.

sections.h2: Taxes, transfer fee and owner-occupied status
sections.html:
• Selling triggers a state transfer fee of $0.50 per $500 of value (SDCL 43-4-21) when something of value is exchanged.
  • Tax comes in two halves. Under SDCL 10-21-23, an unpaid first half is delinquent May 1 and an unpaid second half November 1.
  • Owner-occupied status needs a filing with the Director of Equalization by March 15, and you must own and live in the home on November 1.

Aberdeen follows the statewide formula. Market value is assessed, 85 percent of it is taxed, and the bill reflects the combined levy of county, city and school district.

The state calendar governs appeals, and Brown County posts its dates annually. Assessment notices go out by March 1, with a township informational meeting in early March. After that the pattern is: notice to the local board of equalization about March 12, local boards sitting mid to late March, notice to the county board about April 7, the county board in session April 14 to May 5, and written notice to the Office of Hearing Examiners about May 15.

Court appeals go to circuit court within 30 days of the county board's or hearing examiners' decision. A board that wants to add omitted property or raise an assessment must tell the owner when and where, so the owner can show up or mail proof.

After you accept an offer, a title company reviews ownership, requests the tax payoff from the Brown County Treasurer and prepares the deed. The state transfer fee and recording are handled at closing, and the deed is filed with the Register of Deeds. Whatever tax is still unpaid comes out of your proceeds.

Timing matters in this county. Taxes come due in two halves, and an unpaid first half turns delinquent on May 1, an unpaid second half on November 1. A title transfer must be started before 4:45 p.m. at the Treasurer, so aim to finish paperwork early in the day. If the house is inherited, the signer must be the person with authority over the estate.

sections.h2: Preparing a house for an as-is sale
sections.html:
A cash sale doesn't call for a deep clean or a paint job, but a few small steps still help. Keep the heat on through winter, because frozen pipes cost more than a month of gas. Clear the walkway of snow so we or an inspector can reach the door. Gather any warranties or permit papers, and write down anything you already know is broken, such as a failing furnace or a leaking basement wall.

If belongings are left behind, tell us. We can usually take the house with contents in place, which spares you a cleanout. If a tenant lives there, we can talk about whether they stay or move out on a date that works for everyone. Whatever the situation, tell us early and we will work around it. A short phone call or a few photos usually lets us give a written offer quickly, and nothing is final until you accept it.

sections.h2: Your options for a fast sale
sections.html:
Three paths are open: an agent, a sale by owner, or cash. Listing may fetch the top price, yet it relies on showings, a buyer's loan, an appraisal and repair demands. A cash deal drops those steps and leaves the closing day to you.

We purchase Aberdeen homes as-is. You pay no commission, repair bills or closing costs, and our written offer can sit beside a listing for comparison. Send the address and basics on the house and its occupants; once we have seen it, the choice is yours.

Before talking to any buyer, collect the deed, the newest tax statement and a mortgage payoff if there is one. Landlords add the lease. With an inherited house, decide who signs. The county supplies the tax payoff, and a title company confirms nothing else clings to the property.

faqs.q: How many people live in Aberdeen, SD?
faqs.a: About 27,961 as of July 1, 2025, which is down 1.8% from the April 2020 estimate base of 28,479.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Aberdeen?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes had a median value of $217,300 for 2020-2024, and owners live in 61.7% of homes.

faqs.q: Which office do I call about Aberdeen property taxes?
faqs.a: The Brown County Treasurer, (605) 626-7133, 25 Market St., Suite 2. A question about value goes to the Brown County Director of Equalization.

faqs.q: What is the South Dakota transfer fee when I sell?
faqs.a: Fifty cents per $500 of value, equal to $1.00 per $1,000, set by SDCL 43-4-21 and charged on a deed involving consideration.

faqs.q: Can I sell a vacant Aberdeen house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the city about Nuisance Vacant Building registration first, and then an as-is cash sale needs no repairs or showings.
